The dataviz file format Make your own: by hand, in the builder or with an AI

Open the builder Open a dataviz file Excel template YAML template AI prompt

A dataviz file describes a standard as a graph: its items (chapters, requirements, recommendations...), the links between them, the item and link types, and the filters a reader can tick. The viewer (/view/ of a dataviz site) and the builder (/builder/) read it in the browser: nothing is uploaded, there is no account.

A dataviz file is not the standard itself. To use a standard you have as a PDF, turn it into a dataviz file first, in one of three ways:

  • by hand, from a template: Excel, YAML (commented), JSON, or CSV (items, links);
  • in the builder, item by item, with a live preview;
  • with an AI assistant: give it this prompt and the standard, then open its answer in the builder and check it against the standard (the Check tab lists any problem).

The same content can be written in four carriers, all read the same way: JSON, YAML, Excel (one sheet per table) and CSV (one file per table). A complete example using every feature: example.dataviz.yaml. A JSON Schema for editors and validators: dataviz-file.schema.json.

The smallest file

Only items with an id are required.

items:
  - id: "1"
  - id: "1.1"
    parent: "1"

About the standard

FieldMeaningDefault
datavizFormat version: 11
idShort name used for file names, links and the browser storage: lower case, digits, dashesfrom the title
titleShown at the top of the viewer"Untitled standard"
subtitleOne line under the title
versionVersion of the standard (quote it in YAML: "1.0")
dateDate, YYYY-MM-DD
authorsWho made this file
urlWhere the standard can be read
licenceThe licence of this file (CC-BY-4.0, CC0-1.0, ...). Mind the copyright of any text quoted from a standard
descriptionA few lines, same text syntax as items
layoutauto (saved positions if any, else organic), saved, hierarchical, organic, grid, circleauto
directionFor hierarchical: LR, TB, RL, BTLR

In Excel and CSV these are the rows of the About table, with the columns field and value.

Items

One per chapter, requirement, recommendation, document, test... Table Items.

FieldMeaning
idRequired. Unique. Use the standard's own numbering (5.1-1, ACM-1). In YAML, quote ids that look like numbers
titleThe item's name
typeThe id of a type (below)
parentThe id of the item that contains it. Leave it out at the top level. Parents are drawn as boxes around their children
tagsTag ids (below). A list in JSON and YAML, comma-separated in Excel and CSV
textThe description. One paragraph per line, - starts a bullet, bold, backticks for code, link. Anything else is shown as typed (no HTML)
labelOptional short text drawn on the node, instead of what its type shows
urlOptional link to the item in the standard
x, ySaved position, for the saved layout. The builder fills them in when you arrange the graph

Links

One per arrow. Table Links.

FieldMeaning
fromRequired. Item id where the arrow starts
toRequired. Item id the arrow points to
typeThe id of a link type (below)
labelOptional text on the arrow (the reader can show link labels)

Item types

What each item is, how it looks, and whether it can be assessed. Table Item types.

FieldValuesDefault
idRequired. Referenced by items
labelShown in the legend and the detailsthe id
color#rrggbbautomatic
shaperound-rectangle, rectangle, ellipse, hexagon, diamond, triangle, octagon, tag, barrelround-rectangle
bordersolid, dashed, dotted, double, none. Dashed and dotted draw a light "optional" looksolid
captionWhat the node shows: id, title, bothid
assessyes, no, or empty: items of this type get the self-assessment form (status, justification, evidence, verdict)empty: items without children
descriptionShown as a tooltip in the legend

A type used by an item but not declared is added with default looks (and reported).

Filters and tags

A filter is a group of checkboxes in the viewer's sidebar. Each checkbox is a tag, and items carry the tags that apply to them. Table Filters: one row per tag, with the columns filter, filter label, mode, tag, tag label. Rows with the same filter form one filter.

modeTicking tags...Typical use
any (default)shows the items carrying any ticked tagconditions ("passwords are used")
allshows the items carrying every ticked tagapplicability ("part 1" and "part 2")
nonehides the items carrying a ticked tag"hide recommendations"

Tag ids are unique across all filters. Tags used by items but not declared are gathered in a "Tags" filter (and reported). Several filters combine: an item must pass each one. Parents of a kept item are always drawn, and the reader can also keep the items linked to the kept ones.

In JSON and YAML:

filters:
  - id: condition
    label: Conditions
    mode: any
    tags:
      - id: c1
        label: Passwords are used

Excel and CSV

The workbook has one sheet per table, named About, Item types, Link types, Filters, Items, Links (a Read me sheet is ignored). The first row of each sheet holds the column names, in any order. Unknown columns are ignored, and so are rows whose first cell starts with #. Common spellings are understood: source/target for from/to, kind or category for type, description for text, name for title...

With CSV, give one file per table. Each file is recognised by its name (items.csv, my-standard-links.csv...) or by its columns, so a single file of items is enough to start. Comma, semicolon and tab separators are all read.

What the reader does with it

  • Open it: drop the file on the viewer, or share a link to a file published on the web, with its address after the #: https://<dataviz site>/view/#https://example.org/my-standard.yaml, or for a file in a GitHub repository https://<dataviz site>/view/#gh:owner/repo/my-standard.yaml (#gh:owner/repo@branch/... for another branch). The part after # never reaches the server. The file's server must allow cross-origin reads (GitHub does). Or send a share link copied from the viewer or the builder: it carries the whole file after the #, so it is never sent to any server.
  • Explore it: search, filters, legend, layouts, details of each item and its links.
  • Assess against it: status, justification and evidence per assessable item, an assessor mode with verdicts, kept in the browser and exported as CSV or JSON.

Checks

The viewer and the builder (Check tab) report what they had to fix:

  • errors: an item without id, an id used twice (only the first is drawn), a parent that does not exist or a loop of parents (the item is drawn at the top level), a link to an unknown item (left out), a tag in two filters;
  • warnings: an undeclared type, link type or tag (added), a link to itself, a link listed twice, items with only one coordinate, some items with a saved position and others without.

A file with errors still opens: what can be drawn is drawn.

Versioning

dataviz: 1 is the current format. Future versions will keep reading version 1 files. Unknown fields are ignored by the viewer and are not kept when the builder saves the file.
